dedupe_keys.name: heatshare smart mini district heating with thermal batteries for 36 retirement homes in midlothian sunamp places for people scotland

description: This case study is a vendor-published account of the Heatshare project, in which the existing heating system for 36 retirement homes in Midlothian, Scotland, was refitted as a low-carbon smart mini district heating system. Funded by the SP Energy Networks Green Economy Fund and delivered with Sunamp and the social landlord Places for People Scotland, it combines communal gas boilers, communal air source heat pumps and a Sunamp thermal battery in each home across five micro-scale networks. The page describes the project as the first of its kind in the UK and as a demonstration of the integration of thermal batteries with such networks and of demand side response services for domestic customers. A PassivSystems smart control scans for the cheapest fuel tariffs and switches between gas and electricity to meet each resident's heat demand, charging storage overnight, and existing solar PV feeds the heat pumps. The page reports smaller plantrooms and pipework as a benefit. Access: web page, free. Caveats: vendor-authored, and figures such as carbon savings are estimates from the page. It suits optimisation and control studies of heat network flexibility and fuel poverty, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
